prompt: Value two certain cash flows: USD 5 exactly one year from valuation and USD 105 exactly two years from valuation. Use a flat 5% effective annual discount rate, annual compounding, and PV=sum(CF_t/(1+r)^t). Ignore accrued interest, taxes, and transaction costs. Then reprice at 6% and report shocked PV minus initial PV in USD, with a short explanation. Do not infer a market forecast.
mandatory_criteria: Apply the supplied annual-compounding formula to both cash flows at each rate.
Report both PVs and shocked-minus-initial change within reference tolerances.
Explain why the value falls when the discount rate rises, holding cash flows fixed.
critical_errors: Reverse the sign of shocked-minus-initial change.
Treat the 1 percentage-point shock as a 1% relative rate increase.

calibration_questions.proposition: The supplied formula uses annual compounding.
A continuous-compounding formula directly implements the specified method.
The supplied data are sufficient for the requested deterministic valuation.

critical_errors: Invert the supplied quote while retaining the original units.
